name: example-layout-composition
body:
Load-time example layout composition: the example check — templates-dir-validation step 7 — executes each template's layout against the layout set its layer validates against rather than that layout's text alone. A library layout's name is its layer-relative forward-slash path: `slides/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl` for a slide layout and `sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl` for a section layout — the same string on Windows, macOS and Linux and wherever the layer sits on disk, never a layer root, a `templates/` prefix, a drive letter, a backslash or an absolute path. The external layer is validated on its own before the merge, so its namespace holds only that external layer's layouts — each of its slide layouts and section layouts, keyed by that layer's own layer-relative layout name — and an external-layer layout's `{{ template "<name>" . }}` call naming a local-layer layout is a templates error at that layer's own load. The local layer defers these checks to the merged run, so its namespace holds every layout text the merged library contributes — each slide layout and each section layout, whichever layer carries it — parsed into one html/template namespace keyed by that layer-relative layout name, and a local layout's `{{ template "<name>" . }}` call resolves the named external library layout exactly as it resolves against the render-time shared namespace (template-language, library-layer-references). The merged namespace keys each layout by its layer-relative name, so a local-layer layout invokes an external-layer layout by the target's own layer-relative name (for example `{{ template "sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl" . }}`), and the cross-layer name uniqueness (library-layer-uniqueness) makes that name unambiguous. The namespace is built with the example-checked template's own function map and its own owning layer's `media` sub-filesystem, so every layout in the namespace — the example-checked layout itself and any layout it invokes with `{{ template }}` — resolves its `media` helper in the example-checked template's own owning layer, matching the render-time per-layer namespaces (library-layer-references): html/template fixes the function set for the whole namespace when the namespace is parsed. The `section` helper is the load-time example helper, so a `{{ section "<name>" }}` call renders its target at step 7 instead of failing, and the section target's own layout is re-parsed with the target's own owning layer's `media`, so the target's references resolve in the target's own layer. A `{{ template }}` call naming no layout in the namespace fails step 7 with a file:line-qualified templates error (template-language, templates-dir-validation). This holds for a single-layer library and for a two-layer library: the external layer's example run holds only its own layouts, and the local layer's example run holds the merged set.

AC: a layout that invokes another library layout names it by the target's layer-relative layout name, e.g. `{{ template "slides/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl" . }}`; the example check executes the invoked layout's markup at step 7; the named layout resolves whether it is a slide layout (`slides/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl`) or a section layout (`sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl`), and the same name holds on every OS and wherever the layer sits on disk; in a two-layer library a local-layer layout resolves an external-layer layout by the external layer's own layer-relative name, while an external-layer layout naming a local-layer layout fails step 7 for the external layer's own standalone run; the example-checked layout's own `{{ media "<path>" }}` and every `{{ media }}` in a layout it invokes with `{{ template }}` resolve in the example-checked template's own owning layer; a layout calling `{{ section "<name>" }}` executes its target at step 7 with the target's own owning layer's `media`; a `{{ template }}` call naming no layout in the namespace fails step 7 with a file:line-qualified templates error.
